ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CD \perp AB$ at $D$, $AD=9$, $CD=6$, then what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $CD\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADC=\angle CDB=90^\circ$, $\angle A+\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD+\angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle A=\angle BCD$,\\
therefore $\triangle ADC\sim \triangle CDB$,\\
therefore $\frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{CD}{BD}$,\\
since $AD=9, CD=6$,\\
it follows that $\frac{9}{6}=\frac{6}{BD}$,\\
therefore $BD=\boxed{4}$.
